stories.headline: LLMs get on‑demand memory manager
stories.body: **Dynamic recall, on demand:** MemPilot lets LLM agents pick between cheap generic retrieval and costly targeted delegation, balancing performance, cost, and latency.
stories.why: It lets your agents trade speed for accuracy without rewiring the whole system.

stories.headline: Reflection releases 501B parameter model
stories.body: **Size matters, apparently:** Beam is Reflection’s new open‑weight model packing 501 billion parameters, instantly becoming one of the largest publicly available.
stories.why: Huge models are now accessible for research without a corporate firewall.

stories.headline: Heterogeneous supercloud speeds up analytics
stories.body: **ARM + AI accelerator:** The ReDSEa tool‑chain speeds Dense Cholesky 17× and SVD 88× on a Kunpeng‑920 CPU paired with an Ascend‑910 AI chip.
stories.why: Your data pipelines can shave minutes off heavy linear algebra jobs.

**Tag editor 3.0:** Picard moves to Qt6, adds plugins and ISRC support.
**Speech model buzz:** Phonon‑2 hits 3,063 downloads, 239 likes on Hugging Face.

highlights.title: MemPilot: Orchestrating On-Demand Multimodal Memory Curation for LLM Agents
highlights.summary: MemPilot is a reinforcement‑learning framework that orchestrates on‑demand memory curation for LLM agents, letting them choose between query‑agnostic retrieval and query‑specific delegation according to performance‑cost‑latency preferences.
highlights.detail: Existing agent memory systems preprocess all information regardless of the query, incurring unnecessary cost and potentially discarding useful details. MemPilot introduces a multi‑step LLM policy that dynamically adapts memory handling at runtime. This flexible control aims to balance latency, computational expense, and retrieval quality across varied tasks.

related.title: TokenCast: Forecasting Token Consumption During LLM Agent Execution

highlights.title: BazaarBench: Delegation Safety in Decentralized C2C Marketplaces Run by LLM Agents
highlights.summary: BazaarBench is a simulated consumer‑to‑consumer marketplace benchmark that measures safety of LLM agents by tracking ownership, item condition, and commitments, identifying six failure types across five transaction stages.
highlights.detail: The benchmark runs three base markets for 30 days with inventories drawn from a public eBay sample, then creates 45 continuations where five models are tested under normal, deadline‑pressured, and adversarial instructions. Each continuation spans seven simulated days, allowing analysis of how instruction style affects agent safety and trust outcomes.

highlights.title: Learning to Read the Contextual Tokens in Diffusion Transformers
highlights.summary: The authors train a lightweight bottleneck network that maps diffusion‑transformer contextual tokens into a frozen LLM’s input space, enabling natural‑language interrogation of the image generation process.
highlights.detail: By projecting intermediate tokens to the LLM, the method reveals that these tokens encode a global scene representation, exposing generation‑specific semantics early in denoising. The approach shows that fine‑grained visual details emerge progressively, offering a new way to probe multimodal diffusion models without altering their weights.

highlights.title: Falcon-Emirati: When an LLM Learns the Dialect, the Culture, and the Nuance
highlights.summary: Falcon‑Emirati is a Falcon‑based large language model fine‑tuned on Emirati Arabic dialect data to capture regional language, cultural references, and nuanced expressions.
highlights.detail: The model extends the Falcon family by incorporating corpora specific to the United Arab Emirates, improving relevance for local users. It aims to support applications such as chatbots, content creation, and translation that require culturally aware Arabic output.

highlights.title: Beam: Reflection's 501B open-weight model
highlights.summary: Beam is Reflection’s newly released open‑weight model with 501 billion parameters.
highlights.detail: The model is made publicly available for research and development, offering a scale comparable to the largest proprietary LLMs. Its release enables broader experimentation with extremely large transformer architectures without licensing constraints.

items.title: Building advertising for the way people use AI
items.summary: OpenAI adds a visual ad format to ChatGPT and expands measurement tools, attribution partnerships, and brand‑suitability controls for advertisers.
items.detail: The new format lets advertisers embed images directly within chat interactions, while the enhanced analytics provide deeper insight into ad performance. Partnerships with measurement firms aim to improve attribution accuracy, and brand‑suitability filters help ensure ads align with user expectations.

items.title: Our approach to EU text provenance rules
items.summary: OpenAI details its text watermarking strategy to comply with EU provenance rules, explaining where watermarks are applied, how detection works, and that researcher access is prioritized.
items.detail: The approach aims to embed identifiable signals in generated text to satisfy regulatory transparency. Detection relies on statistical analysis of token patterns. OpenAI positions the system as a safeguard for downstream users while allowing early academic access.

items.title: Model: FermionResearch/Phonon-2
items.summary: The Phonon-2 automatic speech recognition model on Hugging Face has been downloaded 3,063 times and received 239 likes.
items.detail: Phonon-2 targets high-accuracy speech-to-text conversion and is part of the HF trending list. Its popularity reflects interest in open-source ASR solutions, though performance metrics are not listed.

items.title: Model: autotrust/GEV-26B-Decide
items.summary: autotrust's GEV-26B-Decide text‑classification model on Hugging Face shows 446,527 downloads and 507 likes.
items.detail: The 26‑billion‑parameter model is positioned for decision‑making tasks. Its high download count indicates strong community adoption, while the like count suggests positive reception.

items.title: Model: autotrust/JEV-27B-VL
items.summary: autotrust's JEV-27B-VL image‑text‑to‑text model on Hugging Face has accumulated 1,278,569 downloads and 817 likes.
items.detail: JEV-27B-VL combines vision and language capabilities for multimodal generation. The download volume places it among the most accessed multimodal models on the platform.

items.title: [$] An update on the Sashiko patch-review system
items.summary: The Sashiko patch‑review system, which uses an LLM to auto‑generate kernel code reviews, is now an established part of kernel development after its 2026 Kernel Recipes presentation.
items.detail: Sashiko aims to alleviate the bottleneck of manual review by providing preliminary feedback, allowing human reviewers to focus on complex changes. Its adoption reflects growing confidence in AI‑assisted development workflows.

items.title: Picard 3.0 released
items.summary: MusicBrainz Picard 3.0 tag editor was released, upgrading to Qt6, adding a new plugin system, UI tweaks, improved cover‑art processing, and ISRC submission support.
items.detail: The major version bump introduces a modern toolkit and extensibility framework, facilitating third‑party extensions. Enhanced cover‑art handling and ISRC features streamline metadata management for large music collections.

items.title: RustConf recordings
items.summary: The Rust Foundation released recordings and photos from RustConf 2026 in Montreal, with LWN covering four of the talks.
items.detail: The recordings make the conference content accessible to developers who could not attend. The four LWN‑selected talks provide a curated view of the event's highlights, useful for staying current with Rust ecosystem developments.

items.title: Security updates for Monday
items.summary: Security updates were issued on Monday for multiple Linux distributions, covering dozens of packages such as ghostscript, linux‑6.12, chromium, and python‑3.12.
items.detail: The updates span AlmaLinux, Debian, Fedora, Red Hat, and SUSE, addressing vulnerabilities in libraries, runtimes, and applications. Administrators should apply them promptly to maintain system integrity across heterogeneous environments.

items.title: 3D-Printed Filter Removes Most Microplastics From Water
items.summary: A 3D‑printed water filter has been shown to remove the majority of microplastic particles from contaminated water.
items.detail: The filter leverages a printable porous matrix that captures polymer fragments while allowing water flow. This low‑cost approach could be deployed in small‑scale remediation projects, though long‑term durability remains to be evaluated.

items.title: A New Type of LLM on the Block: Decision-Making Models
items.summary: A new class of large language models is being built to make decisions or classifications rather than generate text.
items.detail: These decision‑making LLMs integrate output layers that map internal representations to discrete actions, enabling use cases like routing, policy enforcement, or automated triage. The approach aims to reduce post‑processing steps required by traditional text‑only models.

items.title: Acceleration of Data Analytics on Heterogeneous Supercloud Systems
items.summary: The ReDSEa tool‑chain achieved up to 17× speedup for Dense Cholesky and 88× for SVD on a system with a Huawei Kunpeng 920 ARM CPU and an Ascend 910 AI accelerator.
items.detail: Performance gains stem from automated mapping, load balancing, and novel LLVM‑based compiler optimizations that overlap computation across CPU and AI accelerator. The results surpass a fully optimized 48‑core CPU baseline, demonstrating the potential of heterogeneous superclouds for analytics workloads.

items.title: A Complete, Formal Semantics for Rust Source Code
items.summary: A modular formal semantics for a large subset of Rust source code, including async features and the Tokio runtime, has been defined and proved sound for deductive verification.
items.detail: The semantics separates local expression evaluation from global trace composition, enabling reasoning about fairness of Tokio's scheduler. Soundness proofs connect the semantics to a Rust program logic, facilitating verification of concurrent and asynchronous Rust programs.

related.title: RLX: A Unified Multi-Backend Tensor Compiler and Distributed Runtime in Rust

items.title: Serve Now or Improve Later? Scheduling Self-Evolution in Online Agent Systems
items.summary: LearnSched is a state-aware scheduler that models the trade‑off between self‑evolution compute and immediate service, using one‑step counterfactual rollouts to decide progress, checkpointing, or waiting.
items.detail: The scheduler incorporates candidate progress, checkpoint overhead, and the current recovery path into its action values, aiming to maximize the reuse window of newly created capabilities while minimizing idle compute time. It operates under the same information and capacity constraints as existing systems, but adds a formal investment model to guide decisions.

items.title: From a Last-Week Add-On to First-Day Practice: Three Years of Integrating MPI Performance Analysis into HPC Education with EduMPI Suite
items.summary: EduMPI Suite was integrated over three years into an HPC curriculum, moving performance analysis from a final‑week add‑on to a core component, with all surveyed students recommending early introduction.
items.detail: The suite automates cluster execution, measurement, and near‑real‑time analysis while visualizing MPI communication from the first program, reducing tool and workflow complexity. Survey data from 2025 and unpublished historical evidence show a shift in perception from difficulty to usefulness, supporting its broader adoption in parallel programming courses.

items.title: Hybrid Classical-Quantum Solutions to Accelerate the Adoption of Quantum Computing
items.summary: The paper surveys software stacks for hybrid classical‑quantum computing, listing algorithms, full‑stack libraries, simulators, and cloud providers that are central to building such systems.
items.detail: It examines cloud applications, middleware frameworks, and API gateways that enable classical and quantum resources to interoperate, and outlines an agenda for future research on integration, performance, and usability of hybrid solutions.

items.title: No More Translation at Runtime: LLM-Empowered Static Binary Translation
items.summary: A new static assembly‑to‑assembly translation approach creates native‑like AArch64 binaries from x86‑64 code without runtime frameworks, aiming for portable, efficient execution.
items.detail: The method addresses reliability issues of prior static translators and the runtime overhead of dynamic ones, leveraging recent advances in binary analysis to produce binaries that run on AArch64 devices with performance and energy benefits.

items.title: DuarteSantos8/openGym
items.summary: openGym is a self‑hosted gym and body‑weight tracker that lets users plan routines, log workouts, view muscle usage, and import data from other fitness apps.
items.detail: Features include passkey login, tracking of supersets, warm‑ups, cardio, and the ability to see which muscles are fatigued or detrained, all stored on the user's own server for privacy.

items.title: achillean/shodan-python
items.summary: shodan-python is the official Python client library for the Shodan search engine.
items.detail: The library provides programmatic access to Shodan's API, enabling developers to query internet‑connected device data directly from Python applications.

items.title: boykopovar/AnyPS5
items.summary: Tool for automatically porting PS5 executables to Linux and Windows.
items.detail: The utility streamlines cross‑platform compatibility for games originally built for the PlayStation 5, handling binary translation and necessary runtime adjustments without requiring manual code changes.

items.title: gumyr/build123d
items.summary: Python library that enables programmatic CAD modeling.
items.detail: It offers a high‑level API for constructing 3D geometry, supporting parametric designs and export to common formats, making it suitable for scripting complex parts and integrating with other Python tools.

items.title: M-Abozaid/esp32-c3-adblock
items.summary: Pi‑hole‑class DNS ad‑blocker runs on a $2 ESP32‑C3 using 537 k domain hashes.
items.detail: The system stores domain hashes as 40‑bit FNV‑1a values in flash memory and performs binary search for fast lookups. It provides a UDP DNS sinkhole and a lightweight web dashboard for management.

items.title: VictorTaelin/OptMem
items.summary: Provides permanent memory for AI agents via a 426‑token prompt script, plug‑and‑play.
items.detail: The package lets agents retain context across interactions without external storage, embedding the memory directly in the prompt. It is delivered as a simple Python script that can be integrated into existing agent pipelines.
